title: Tempo Safety Lane: Remediation Flow and Selective Backport Spec
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Create a reproducible, low-latency remediation flow we call 'Tempo Safety Lane' for handling regressions that require immediate patches, targeted backports into LTS and stable channels, and automated rollback where appropriate. This ticket defines severity criteria, branch/PR conventions, automated cherry-pick/backport tooling integration, canary gating rules, and post-release validation for hot patches and rollbacks. The flow must minimize blast radius, reduce human error in backports, and integrate with the Console dashboards and incident runbooks.
background: We currently have ad-hoc hotfix procedures scattered across runbooks. Past incidents showed inconsistent branch naming, missed backports to maintained LTS branches, and manual cherry-picks that caused merge conflicts during a high-severity outage. Tempo Safety Lane formalizes decisions and adds automation to reduce cognitive load on the on-call release engineer.
severity_matrix: Severity 1 (S1) - Service outage/blocker: total regression for core inference paths, >5% customer-error budget burn in 10m, or data loss. Action: Immediate hot patch, create emergency patch branch, notify execs, invoke paged incident playbook.

Severity 2 (S2) - Degraded correctness or performance: high latency regressions impacting SLAs (>2x p95 increase) or significant quality regression in model outputs affecting major customers. Action: Hot patch or rapid rollback to last-known-good image and schedule targeted backports.

Severity 3 (S3) - Minor regressions: non-blocking errors, cosmetic issues, non-critical telemetry anomalies. Action: Plan a normal patch in next sprint; consider fast-follow backport for specific customers.
Severity 4 (S4) - Non-customer visible or internal: low priority; address in normal cadence.
branch_strategy: Single-source-of-truth: hot patches must be branched from the exact commit SHA that matched the deployed release (tagged). Avoid branching from main except for forward-merges.

Patch branch lifecycle: create -> PR with changelog + metrics -> automated CI (unit + smoke + runtime-fast) -> gated canary -> rollout or rollback -> backport PRs created and tracked -> merge -> close branch.

Backport targets: maintain a backport matrix per release: e.g., 2.4.x (LTS), 2.3.x (maintenance), and main. Only backport when customer_impact >= medium or when regression affects maintained API compatibility.
Backport policy: select 'selective backport'—not all fixes are backported. Required for security/S1 S2 with customer impact high, optional for S3 at discretion of release lead.
automation_and_tools: Backport Bot: extend backport-bot to support 'selective backport' labels and 'target-channel' metadata. Bot creates draft PRs against configured maintained branches and attaches build artifacts and reproduction steps.
Cherry-pick helper: a CLI command 'tempo backport' that validates patch applicability, runs a dry-run cherry-pick in a disposable workspace, and reports conflicts ahead of human review.
PR templates: standardized emergency PR template capturing deployed-suffix SHA, telemetry links, minimal reproducer, and canary validation checklist.
Auto-tagging: merged hot patches must include metadata tags: severity, patch-commit, incident-id (if any), and backport-status, appended to the release changelog automatically.
Dashboard hooks: a 'remediation' view in Console that surfaces active patch branches, canary cohorts, and SLO delta charts for the last 60 minutes.
canary_and_gating: Canary cohort size: default 2% of traffic or 10 nodes (whichever is larger) for production; internal-only flags for staged environments.

Health signals: error-rate (5xx), p95 latency, user-facing incorrectness (evaluations), and token-generation failures. Thresholds preconfigured per severity: S1 triggers immediate halt at 1% error increase; S2 triggers review at 0.5%.
Automated gates: if any gate fails, the rollout system must either automatically rollback to previous image or pause and notify release lead depending on severity and config.
Manual override: release engineer can opt into 'manual proceed' only after providing justification in PR and notifying stakeholders. Overrides must be audited.
rollback_playbook: Step 0 - Triage: Confirm impact and trigger severity classification. Obtain deployed-SHA and list of affected routes.
Step 1 - Isolate: Roll partial traffic away if possible (region or customer-tier routing) to limit blast radius.
Step 2 - Decide: For S1/S2, prefer rollback to last-known-good image if patch is not trivial. For targeted correctness fixes where rollback causes more harm, proceed with hot patch.
Step 3 - Execute: Use orchestration to revert to tagged image and monitor canary for 15 minutes. If successful, promote rollback globally. Record incident-id in rollback PR.
Step 4 - Post-rollback actions: Create follow-up PRs for permanent fix, attach postmortem stub, and set owners for backporting where needed.
Escalation: if rollback fails or leads to further degradation, escalate to SRE lead and open incident commander thread.
testing_and_validation: Fast runtime validation: a smoke harness that runs a small suite of representative prompts across the affected models and checks latency, top-k token stability, and KV-cache integrity.
Repro harness: reproduction scripts stored in repo under /runbooks/remediation/repro that can be executed by CI during PR validation.
Backport test matrix: backport PRs must run the same minimal smoke tests plus branch-merge CI to catch cross-branch conflicts.
roles_and_ownership: Release engineer (on-call): owns branch creation, canary orchestration, and merge decisions for emergency patches during the shift.
Service owner / model-owner: provides correctness acceptance and signs off on any forward promotion of hot patches.
SRE: monitors SLOs, executes rollback orchestration when triggered by automated gates.
Security reviewer: required boolean approval for any patch affecting KMS/HSM, telemetry, or authentication flows.
acceptance_criteria: Clear severity matrix documented and shared with SRE/PM/Eng
Backport-bot updated with 'selective backport' targets and creates draft PRs automatically
CLI helper 'tempo backport' merged and available in release-infra with conflict dry-run
Console remediation dashboard prototypes surfaced for release lead and SRE to review
At least one simulated S1 runbook rehearsal completed end-to-end in staging with rollback validated
risks_and_migration_notes: Risk: Over-automating backports may produce noisy draft PRs for irrelevant branches; mitigated via strict target matrix and 'opt-in' labels.
Risk: Rollback to earlier images can regress forward-facing data migrations. For data-affecting releases, prefer patch-in-place strategy with feature flips.
Migration: we will pilot Tempo Safety Lane on runtime-2.4 and extend to other product teams after 4-week stabilization.
